## What it is

A single audited policy row — `{ mode: 'enforce' | 'off', allowHarnesses: string[] (globs: `papercusp`, `papercusp/*`), exceptions? }` — that every dispatch chokepoint consults through `gateWorkScope(site, { harness, plan?, goal?, workItem? })` in `packages/operator-core/lib/work-scope-policy.ts`. There is NO shadow / log-only mode and no dark flag (plan D-001): with no row, or `mode:'off'`, every gate is one cached read returning `allowed:'no-policy'` — byte-identical behaviour. Landing the code changes nothing until an owner-directed `set`.

## Control surface (D-003)

`workspace:work_scope { op:'get' | 'check' | 'set' | 'clear' }` (`agent-tools/pot/work-scope.ts`). `set`/`clear` run the shared audited mutation `applyWorkScopeSet` / `applyWorkScopeClear` in `packages/operator-core/lib/work-scope-control.ts` (`runControlMutation`, pot-control-policy revisions, audit id `gwc-…`); reversal is ONE `clear`. `get` returns the policy + the bounded `scope_decisions` ledger (ring cap 100) with counts (denied/held/rehomed). `check { harness }` evaluates the live policy for one harness — the replicable probe for any grader.

**The :3170 door.** A tool that is not yet on green `main` is invisible to `tools:invoke` from an su session (served by :3070). Until the green-checkpoint gate promotes it, call it on staging: write the args to a file and run `node scripts/mcp-call.mjs workspace:work_scope --json-file /tmp/ws.json --client <your-su-id> --port 3170`. A papercusp-scoped session may also need explicit `--harness <slug>` for `check`. The same door serves `state:read` for the cell below.

## Reading it: the `workspace.workScope` state cell (WI-2145092)

`state:read { cell:'workspace.workScope' }` answers "is this workspace confined right now, and to which harnesses?" without calling the tool: headline `mode`; assessment at `assessments.policy` ∈ `enforce` (out-of-scope work is refused at every seam) / `off` (a row exists but confines nothing — mode off, or an enforce row with an empty allow-list) / `absent` (no row, D-001 byte-identical), with evidence paths `enforced` + `allowHarnesses`; `state:subscribe` on it to be woken by a flip (changeSignal: poll `workspace:work_scope_status`, path `mode`). The CellSpec is `WORK_SCOPE_CELL` in `packages/operator-core/lib/cell-registrations.ts`.

It is resolved through the READ-ONLY lens `workspace:work_scope_status` (`agent-tools/pot/work-scope-status.ts`, capability `intel:read`), never through the control tool: the cell dispatcher (`dispatchReadOnlyTool`) refuses any resolver whose projected effect is not `read`, so a write-capable control tool cannot back a cell — a sibling read-only lens is the pattern (`governor:state_snapshot` is the precedent). The lens is `buildWorkScopeStatusPayload(readWorkScopePolicy())` in `work-scope-policy.ts`; `assessWorkScope` is the pure classifier and folds mode + allow-list through the SAME `isWorkScopeEnforced` predicate the gates use, so a reader branches on exactly what is enforced.

Adding a cell moves pins: `BUILTIN_CELLS` length and the PAYLOADLESS name list in `cell-assessment-reality.test.ts`, the cell list in `cell-registrations.test.ts`, and the per-visibility census in `cell-access-parity` (workspace 13 → 14 for this cell).

## The /admin door (WI-2145092, the D-003 residue)

`/admin/work-scope` — AdminShell tab **Work scope**. One path, two doors:

- **Read:** sync query `workScope.policy` (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts`, backing table `operator_pot_control_policy`), the SAME status payload the cell and the MCP lens return, so the pane, the cell and the tool cannot disagree. It is SSE-invalidated on every set/clear through the `OPERATOR_STATE_SYNC_NAMES` bridge in `operator-state-pg.ts`.
- **Write:** `POST /api/work-scope/set { mode, allowHarnesses, reason }` and `POST /api/work-scope/clear` (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/work-scope/set.ts`, registered in `routes/index.ts`): loopback-only, actor `admin:<principal>`, run through the same `applyWorkScopeSet` / `applyWorkScopeClear` mutation as the MCP tool, so every pane write is audited identically; a failed revert answers `ok:false` with 502.

**Where the pane actually lives (the EI-46 trap, hit again here).** The desktop renders the operator-vite SPA with an explicit TanStack route tree: the door is `apps/operator-vite/src/routes/admin/work-scope.tsx` (`createFileRoute('/admin/work-scope')` composing the Vite `components/admin/AdminShell` around the component) plus the `{ href:'/admin/work-scope', label:'Work scope' }` entry in `apps/operator-vite/src/components/admin/AdminShell.tsx` (its tab rail is pinned by `AdminShell.test.tsx` — update `TAB_HREFS` and the label list together). The component itself is `apps/operator/app/admin/work-scope/WorkScopeAdmin.tsx`, reached through the `@/app` alias; the `page.tsx` + Next AdminShell tab beside it are the retired-Next twin and, on their own, leave the path rendering the SPA fallback (measured 2026-09-05: `tauri-agent-tools navigate /admin/work-scope` showed the Accounts page until the Vite route existed). `routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by the router plugin on every build and gitignored, so a new route reaches the shared `dist` on the fleet's next `vite build --watch` pass, not on save.

The pane shows the assessment (`data-testid="work-scope-assessment"`), allow-list chips (`work-scope-allow`), setBy/reason/updatedAt, ledger counts (`work-scope-count-denied`) and the recent ledger table; the form needs a reason of ≥3 chars and clear is a two-step confirm. Form drafts are `useState` by the nuqs rule (mid-edit drafts, no URL-meaningful selection).

Verify it headlessly, never in a browser and never on the owner's window: `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh -- bash <assert.sh>` where the script runs `tauri-agent-tools navigate --pid "$VERIFY_TAURI_PID" /admin/work-scope`, polls `eval` for `[data-testid="work-scope-admin"]`, then `check --pid "$VERIFY_TAURI_PID" --selector … --eval … --no-errors` and `capture` (export `DISPLAY="$VERIFY_TAURI_DISPLAY"` first — the screenshot leg shells out to xdotool). `tauri-agent-tools` without `--pid` is refused by a target guard, even for `--help`, because the first bridge it finds may be the owner's live desktop. The DB is the LIVE workspace DB unless `VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1`, so a read-only assertion pass must not click Set/Clear.

## The 9 dispatch seams (grep `gateWorkScope(`)

`agent-tools/work_items/claim.ts` · `work_items/claim_next.ts` · `plan-items/claim.ts` · `scheduler/get_next.ts` · `capability/launch-agent.ts` · `fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts` · `harness/git-sync/git-sync-action.ts` (merge-resolver / content-fixer dispatch) · `harness/routines/release-actions.ts` (`dispatchReleaseFixer`) · `packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/goals/pots.ts` (`goals:attach-pot`). Plus the non-dispatch holds: the admission promoter (`runWorkItemAdmissionPromoter` early-returns for an out-of-scope harness; the workspace-wide fail-open UPDATE carries `workScopeSqlTerms`), and the plan-drain / acceptance-drain sweeps skip out-of-scope rows. A refusal is `{ ok:false, code:'scope_denied', message }`.

## Held, never deleted (D-002, D-004)

An out-of-scope work-item keeps `admission:'pending'` — no new admission value, no migration — stays visible in /admin/admission AND in the unclaimed-work-digest (the digest builder `harness/routines/unclaimed-work-digest-action.ts` carries no scope filter on purpose: the digest describes, the gates refuse), and becomes claimable the moment the policy widens.

## Loudness (P-011)

`recordWorkScopeDecision` appends every deny/hold/re-home to the ledger (a ledger write failure never changes the verdict) and, outside VITEST, `broadcastWorkScopeDecision` sends once per 10 min per `site|harness|verdict` to `['human']` plus an `improvements:capture` observation keyed `scope:<verdict>:<harness>`. Read it with `coord:feed { audience:'human', q:'work-scope' }`, or the ledger counts on the cell / the pane.

## Re-home (P-009)

`work_items:rehome { op:'classify' | 'move', id, harness, reason }` (`agent-tools/work_items/rehome.ts`). `classify` yields keep / rehome / hold — platform-referencing items move, genuinely other-pot work is HELD, never naively moved. `move` updates `work_items` plus `REHOME_DEPENDENT_TABLES` (feature_claims, claim_audit, work_item_blocked, work_item_release_cooldowns, harness_feature_notes, harness_feature_debug_notes, harness_pending_issues, triage_routed_items) keyed by `(workspace_id, harness_slug, feature_id)` in ONE transaction and stamps `payload.rehomed_from`.

## Session homing (D-005)

`reconcilePresencePot`, called from `agent-tools/coordination/presence.ts` `writePresence`, replaces a requested pot that disagrees with the pot derived from `PAPERCUSP_HARNESS_SLUG` and logs the correction. Root cause of the four sb-devboard-hive mis-homed sessions (EI-22374455128414213) was launch-time hive identity [inferred]; the durable fix is the reconcile.

## Caveats

- **Boot prime (EI-22388253359874854):** the first implementation read the pot-control cache, which starts empty in a fresh process and only fills on a later tick — so a freshly started operator allowed everything. `gateWorkScope` now reads the stored row when the cache is cold. A fresh-process `check` denying an out-of-scope harness is the regression probe.
- **Hive guard:** `loop:arm { harness:'papercusp' }` from a session whose presence pot is another hive is refused by the hive floor — fix the presence pot (the reconcile does it on the next write), do not re-arm around it.
- **Rubric hygiene learned shipping this:** an acceptance-rubric method that shells out to a gitignored scratch file is not gradeable by anyone but its author — use the `check` door; the sole vetting critic is barred from emitting the independent grade; any rubric edit un-counts the independent card, so batch edits before grading.
- **Which host runs the code:** an su session's own MCP calls execute on :3070 (the release build). Until `main` is green, the cell, the status lens, the routes and the pane are exercised on :3170 (`mcp-call --port 3170`) or in the headless Tauri shell, which boots its own sidecar from the working tree. A staging-api restart is unnecessary when every server-side file's mtime (`TZ=UTC stat`) precedes the process start (`dev:service_health` secondsSinceStart).
